The rapid evolution of smart grids, driven by rising global energy demand and renewable energy 
integration, calls for intelligent, adaptive, and energy-efficient resource allocation strategies. 
Traditional energy management methods, based on static models or heuristic algorithms, often 
fail to handle real-time grid dynamics, leading to suboptimal energy distribution, high operational 
costs, and significant energy wastage. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents ORA-DL 
(Optimized Resource Allocation using Deep Learning) an advanced framework that integrates deep 
learning, Internet of Things (IoT)-based sensing, and real-time adaptive control to optimize smart 
grid energy management. ORA-DL employs deep neural networks, reinforcement learning, and 
multi-agent decision-making to accurately predict energy demand, allocate resources efficiently, 
and enhance grid stability. The framework leverages both historical and real-time data for proactive 
power flow management, while IoT-enabled sensors ensure continuous monitoring and low-latency 
response through edge and cloud computing infrastructure. Experimental results validate the 
effectiveness of ORA-DL, achieving 93.38% energy demand prediction accuracy, improving grid 
stability to 96.25%, and reducing energy wastage to 12.96%. Furthermore, ORA-DL enhances resource 
distribution efficiency by 15.22% and reduces operational costs by 22.96%, significantly outperforming 
conventional techniques. These performance gains are driven by real-time analytics, predictive 
modelling, and adaptive resource modulation. By combining AI-driven decision-making, IoT sensing, 
and adaptive learning, ORA-DL establishes a scalable, resilient, and sustainable energy management 
solution. The framework also provides a foundation for future advancements, including integration 
with edge computing, cybersecurity measures, and reinforcement learning enhancements, marking a 
significant step forward in smart grid optimization.

The surge increase of the global population and the increasing usage of renewable energy sources across countries 
has resulted in an efficient power management system to be put in place and has also created more complex systems 
to be designed1–4. The dynamic nature of energy demand, coupled with the increasing integration of renewable 
energy sources, presents significant challenges in smart grid resource allocation. Existing approaches primarily 
rely on static models or heuristic-based methods, which fail to adapt to real-time fluctuations in grid conditions. 
Traditional resource allocation methods suffer from inefficiencies such as suboptimal energy distribution, high 
operational costs, and limited adaptability to grid variability. Moreover, many existing techniques lack predictive 
capabilities, leading to excessive energy wastage and reactive rather than proactive decision-making. Smart grids 
that are powered by AI and the IoT expand the possibilities for energy management by facilitating monitoring, 
decision making and resource allocation in real time and subsequently increasing resource use efficiency5 IoT 
enabled smart grids enhance data collection, communication, control, and even data processing which improves 
energy distribution and efficiency6–8. However, these new developments are challenged by legacy methods 
of allocating resources which still causes ineffective energy distribution, expensive operational spending, 
and inflexible adaption to the changing conditions of the grid9,10. Several existing methodologies attempt to 
address resource allocation in smart grids, including deep reinforcement learning (DRL), machine learning 
(ML)-based optimization, and IoT-driven energy management systems11–13. However, these approaches exhibit 
various shortcomings. DRL-based models often require extensive training and high computational resources, 
making real-time implementation challenging. ML-based energy optimization techniques are largely dependent 
on historical data and lack the ability to dynamically adjust to real-time grid fluctuations. IoT-enabled smart 
grids, while effective in data acquisition and monitoring, often lack an integrated decision-making mechanism 
to optimize energy distribution efficiently14,15. These limitations highlight the need for a more advanced and 
adaptive framework to enhance smart grid performance. These issues highlight the gap for deploying novel 
energy allocation methods using deep learning whilst ensuring grid stability and data driven ways of achieving 
maximum utility out of a single value16.
Deep learning, a subset of artificial intelligence, has showed an overwhelming capability to solve complex 
problems using high level data analysis using multiple datasets17,18. Using deep learning as a technique 
within smart grids may facilitate the energy estimation, improve resource allocation, and enhance the overall 
reliability of the system19. Smart grids using deep learning and IoT-based energy management systems may 
minimize energy waste by dynamically allocating resources based on real-time data20,21. However, the same 
approaches attract more attention than only computational complexity, scalability, and grid adaptation22. To 
address these challenges, this work introduces ORA-DL, an intelligent deep learning-based framework designed 
for optimal resource allocation in smart grids. ORA-DL integrates real-time analytics, predictive modeling, 
and reinforcement learning to dynamically allocate resources while ensuring grid stability and operational 
efficiency. Unlike traditional methods, ORA-DL continuously learns from both historical and real-time energy 
consumption patterns, enabling a proactive energy management strategy. The proposed framework significantly 
reduces energy wastage, enhances grid resilience, and lowers operational costs, making it a scalable and 
economically viable solution for modern smart grid infrastructures. To address these difficulties, it offers the 
ORA-DL framework, which uses smart grid deep learning to boost grid efficiency23. ORA-DL predicts energy 
demand, optimizes resource allocation, and stabilizes the grid using real-time data analysis and powerful 
machine learning24. The platform learns from previous, real-time, and changing supply and demand energy 
trends to maintain grid balance and efficiency25. ORA-DL uses deep learning to regulate resources, save costs, 
and eliminate energy losses in smart grid decision-making26. ORA-DL may boost energy economy without 
compromising grid resilience27. Older policies may utilize allocation models that use averages to alter supply 
depending on energy demand.
ORA-DL uses predictive analysis to dynamically distribute energy to maximize resource consumption 
while maintaining grid structural integrity28. The system also facilitates demand-side control, allowing users 
to maximize cheap and eco-friendly energy usage29. Average ORA-DL experimental findings show increased 
system resilience, energy economy improvement, and lower operating cost than other traditional techniques. 
It integrates IoT, real-time analytics, and deep learning to overcome significant smart grid management 
challenges and provide a more powerful and adaptable energy distribution system30. It presents ORA-DL design, 
implementation, and performance studies for smart grid optimization. This article highlights energy-efficient 
IoT and deep learning-based smart grid applications’ problems and future research. It advances sustainable 
power management in smart networks by reducing energy waste and ensuring electricity supply continuity. The

ORA-DL framework introduces a novel deep learning-based approach to optimize resource allocation, energy 
demand forecasting, and grid stability in smart grids. Unlike traditional methods that rely on static allocation 
models or pre-defined heuristic-based strategies, ORA-DL employs real-time data analytics, adaptive learning, 
and deep reinforcement learning techniques to dynamically distribute energy with higher efficiency and 
accuracy. The proposed framework significantly reduces energy wastage and operational costs while ensuring 
sustainable and intelligent power management.
Justification
The evolving energy landscape, driven by increasing global energy demands and the integration of renewable 
energy sources, has significantly increased the complexity of modern power networks. Traditional energy 
management systems are inherently rigid, inefficient, and costly, lacking the necessary adaptability to respond 
effectively to dynamic grid conditions and fluctuating energy demands. These limitations result in inefficient 
resource allocation, excessive operational costs, and suboptimal energy utilization, which hinder the transition 
toward sustainable and cost-effective power management.
To address these challenges, advanced technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and deep learning 
offer intelligent, data-driven solutions for optimizing energy distribution, improving grid stability, and 
minimizing energy wastage. By leveraging real-time analytics and adaptive learning, deep learning models can 
effectively predict energy demand fluctuations, dynamically allocate resources, and enhance the resilience and 
efficiency of smart grids.
This work introduces ORA-DL, a novel deep learning-based framework specifically designed to optimize 
resource allocation in smart grids. ORA-DL integrates predictive modeling, real-time data processing, and 
adaptive learning mechanisms to ensure efficient energy distribution while maintaining grid reliability and 
operational cost-effectiveness. The proposed system significantly enhances energy efficiency, reduces energy 
wastage, and ensures sustainable power management, making it a scalable and economically viable solution for 
modern smart grid infrastructures.
Problem statement
Existing smart grid resource allocation methodologies suffer from significant inefficiencies, limited adaptability 
to real-time grid fluctuations, and excessive energy consumption. Conventional static energy distribution 
strategies operate on fixed allocation models that lack the ability to dynamically respond to variations in supply 
and demand. As a result, these systems lead to energy imbalances, increased operational costs, and substantial 
resource wastage, ultimately reducing the overall efficiency and sustainability of power management in smart 
grids. To overcome these limitations, this work presents ORA-DL, an intelligent deep learning-based framework 
designed to dynamically optimize resource allocation, predict energy demand with high accuracy, and enhance 
grid stability. Unlike traditional methods, ORA-DL utilizes real-time data analytics and adaptive learning to 
continuously adjust energy distribution based on changing grid conditions, thereby minimizing energy losses, 
improving efficiency, and ensuring a more resilient and cost-effective smart grid infrastructure.
Contribution of this paper
The proposed research introduces the ORA-DL framework, a deep learning-based approach for energy-efficient 
resource allocation in smart grids. The framework is designed to overcome the limitations of traditional static and 
heuristic-based allocation techniques by incorporating real-time data analytics, adaptive learning, and predictive 
modeling. Unlike conventional energy management systems that rely on historical trends, ORA-DL dynamically 
adjusts energy distribution based on real-time demand-supply fluctuations, thereby enhancing grid efficiency and 
reducing wastage. This development forms the core contribution of this study and lays the foundation for further 
advancements. A key component of ORA-DL is its adaptive learning and real-time data processing capability, 
which enables intelligent decision-making and energy distribution optimization. Traditional methods struggle 
with unpredictable grid conditions due to their rigid allocation models. In contrast, ORA-DL continuously 
learns from historical and live data, allowing it to make autonomous energy allocation decisions that maximize 
efficiency while ensuring grid stability. The integration of deep neural networks and reinforcement learning 
techniques further enhances the system’s ability to predict energy consumption patterns with high accuracy, 
reducing operational inefficiencies and improving sustainability. Another major contribution of this work is 
the implementation of a multi-agent intelligent decision-making model, which significantly enhances ORA-
DL’s performance in distributed smart grid environments. Unlike centralized control mechanisms, which often 
lead to bottlenecks and delays, ORA-DL employs a multi-agent system that allows decentralized, autonomous 
decision-making across different grid sectors. This feature enables localized control and faster response to 
dynamic energy demands, ensuring a more resilient and adaptive grid infrastructure. By leveraging IoT-enabled 
monitoring and sensor-driven data collection, the multi-agent system ensures optimal resource allocation with 
minimal intervention. Furthermore, this study provides comprehensive performance validation of ORA-DL 
by comparing its effectiveness against existing machine learning, IoT-based, and deep reinforcement learning 
(DRL) methods for smart grid optimization.

Deep learning-based smart city energy optimization

ML-based smart grid energy optimization
The suggested approach presents a Machine Learning-Based Energy-Efficient Framework analyzing occupant 
motion and generates short-term energy forecasts to maximize the use of renewable energy in smart grids. The 
platform compiles occupant and energy profiles using indoor localization devices and real-time smart meter 
networks, then couples these profiles with forecast data using an online machine learning model35. Through 
effective solar energy allocation, the technique lowers peak demand on the main power grid, therefore improving 
energy forecasting accuracy and resource optimization using little computing resources.
Energy-net forecasting model
The suggested approach presents the Energy-Net model, a deep learning framework intended for temporary 
energy consumption prediction. Stacked spatiotemporal modules, each including a temporal transformer (TT) 
to model load data relationships and a spatial transformer (ST) to extract spatial information via convolutional 
layers and an enhanced self-attention mechanism36 make up the model. Energy-Net offers a computationally 
efficient solution for IoT devices in smart grid applications, according evaluations on the IHPEC and ISO-NE 
datasets, which show Energy-Net beats other models with lesser root mean-square error (RMSE).

Proposed method
The development of smart grids makes it possible to achieve through the integration of the Internet of Things, 
edge computing, and deep learning technologies to ensure powerful energy management. These techniques 
implement sophisticated adaptive decisioning, real-time data ingestion, and powerful analytics to fortify the 
grid, enhance the power distribution system, and minimize energy losses. This change guarantees more efficient 
energy usage and a wider smart grid system with best results in cost effective and eco-friendly sustainable energy 
resources. In the proposed ORA-DL framework, sensor data preprocessing includes noise filtering and missing 
value imputation to ensure reliable input to the predictive models. For noisy data, the system employs statistical 
smoothing techniques such as moving average filters and anomaly detection mechanisms to eliminate outliers 
and measurement errors. In the case of missing sensor values, nearest-neighbour imputation and real-time 
interpolation based on historical patterns are used to reconstruct the data, ensuring continuity and stability of 
decision-making under real-time operational scenarios.

Systems (MAS) a component-wise performance evaluation was conducted. This analysis isolates the effect of 
each module by selectively deactivating one component at a time and observing the change in key performance 
metrics such as energy demand prediction accuracy, grid stability, energy wastage reduction, and operational 
cost savings. The Deep Neural Network (DNN) serves as the primary prediction engine within ORA-DL, and its 
contribution is critical to achieving the high 93.38% prediction accuracy. When the DNN module was replaced 
with a conventional machine learning model (such as Linear Regression), a significant drop of nearly 17–20% 
in prediction accuracy was observed, demonstrating the superior learning capacity of deep architectures in 
capturing complex, nonlinear energy patterns. The Reinforcement Learning (RL) module introduces adaptive 
control mechanisms that dynamically adjust resource allocation policies based on real-time feedback from the 
grid environment. Experimental results indicate that excluding RL from the framework leads to approximately 
a 12% decrease in grid stability and higher fluctuations in resource allocation, confirming RL’s crucial role in 
maintaining system resilience under dynamic conditions. The IoT-based sensing and real-time data acquisition 
layer enhances the responsiveness of the system by providing accurate and timely input data. Without real-time 
IoT integration, the model relies only on historical data, leading to a 9–11% increase in energy wastage due to 
the inability to react promptly to current grid conditions. Finally, the Multi-Agent System (MAS) facilitates 
distributed intelligence, ensuring that local decisions are made effectively across various grid sectors. Disabling 
the multi-agent approach and reverting to a centralized decision-making process resulted in higher latency, 
bottlenecks, and up to a 7–9% reduction in overall resource distribution efficiency.
Computational complexity and scalability analysis
To assess the computational efficiency and scalability of the ORA-DL framework, an analysis was conducted to 
evaluate its performance as the number of grid nodes and IoT-enabled sensors increases. The complexity of the 
deep neural network (DNN)-based prediction module primarily depends on the number of layers (L) and the 
number of neurons (N) in each layer, leading to an approximate time complexity of O(L·N²) for forward and 
backward propagation during the training phase. However, the prediction phase operates at O(L·N) complexity, 
ensuring rapid inference once the model is trained. The reinforcement learning (RL) module introduces 
additional learning complexity, particularly in the exploration phase. However, the use of multi-agent systems 
(MAS) significantly reduces computational overhead by enabling distributed decision-making and localized 
control. This decentralization minimizes bottlenecks and allows the system to maintain performance as the grid 
size expands. Simulation experiments were performed by varying the number of sensors from 100 to 1000 units 
and the number of grid nodes from 10 to 100 sectors. Results indicate that due to the distributed architecture 
and parallel processing enabled by MAS and IoT edge computing, the system maintains less than 15% increase 
in decision latency even with a tenfold increase in sensor volume. These results confirm the scalability and 
computational feasibility of ORA-DL for large-scale smart grid applications.
Contribution of the objective work
The selection of the ORA-DL (Optimized Resource Allocation using Deep Learning) framework for this research 
is driven by the critical need for adaptive, scalable, and intelligent resource allocation strategies that can handle 
real-time grid fluctuations and the integration of renewable energy sources. Conventional optimization methods, 
such as heuristic-based approaches, linear programming (LP), genetic algorithms (GA), and particle swarm 
optimization (PSO), often rely on static decision rules or predefined models. These methods, although effective 
for specific scenarios, lack the adaptability and predictive intelligence required to respond dynamically to rapidly 
changing grid conditions, especially in the presence of intermittent renewable energy inputs. In contrast, the ORA-
DL framework utilizes deep learning models combined with reinforcement learning and multi-agent decision-
making to continuously learn from both historical and real-time data streams. This dynamic learning capability 
enables the framework to proactively adjust energy allocation decisions based on demand-supply variations, 
thus outperforming static allocation models. Compared to machine learning-based energy optimization, which 
often depends on past trends and fails to generalize effectively in non-stationary environments, ORA-DL’s deep 
neural network architecture enhances the prediction accuracy of energy demand patterns. The reinforcement 
learning component within ORA-DL introduces adaptive control by balancing exploration and exploitation, 
ensuring optimal resource distribution while preventing grid instability. A comparative evaluation against 
widely used methods such as IoT-DRL Smart Grid Optimization, ML-Based Energy Optimization, and Energy-
Net Forecasting Models (as summarized in Table 3 of this paper) demonstrates the superior performance of 
ORA-DL. Specifically, ORA-DL achieves 93.38% accuracy in energy demand prediction, 96.25% grid stability, 
a 12.96% reduction in energy wastage, and 22.96% lower operational costs. These results clearly justify the 
choice of ORA-DL over traditional optimization techniques by highlighting its robustness, learning efficiency, 
scalability, and real-time adaptability.
Conclusion
Should smart grids integrating deep learning with energy-efficient Internet of Things (IoT) increase automation, 
better distribute resources, and guarantee grid stability, power management would change dramatically. The 
proposed ORA-DL architecture shows amazing prediction of energy demand and enhances grid stability to 
96.25% with an accuracy of 93.38%. Furthermore, helping to produce a more affordable and sustainable energy 
distribution system are operating expenses by 22.96% and energy waste by 12.96%. Real-time data analytics 
and adaptive learning allow ORA-DL to dynamically allocate resources. Good use of power assures hence little 
possibility of system instability. Apart from its efficiency, the paradigm has major constraints as well. One area
